stem: A Messages API support assistant uses server-side compaction for long chats. The app sends the operator's standing rules (tone, refund limits, when to escalate) as the first user message of each conversation, and there is no system prompt. After compaction triggers, the assistant sometimes stops following those rules. What is the best fix?

options.text: Lower the compaction trigger so that summaries are shorter and more of the early conversation stays verbatim.
options.why: Compacting sooner summarizes the first message sooner; it does not keep the rules word for word.

options.text: Move the standing rules into the system prompt, which is sent with every request and is not part of the compacted messages.
options.why: Compaction replaces older messages with a summary; the system prompt is sent separately on each request, so the rules persist.

options.text: Ask the assistant to restate all of the rules at the start of every reply so a recent copy is always in history.
options.why: This bloats every turn and still relies on model-written copies surviving later summaries.

options.text: Disable compaction and switch to a model with a larger context window so that the first message is never summarized.
options.why: A larger window only delays the limit; long chats still overflow, and the rules remain in the wrong place.

explanation: Compaction summarizes the conversation's older messages, so anything that exists only in early turns can be condensed or lost. Standing rules belong in the system prompt, which the application sends on every request and which compaction does not replace; per-conversation facts that must survive can go in memory or be re-injected after compaction.
reference: Claude API docs — Compaction; Giving Claude a role with a system prompt
source: Gap fill: candidate-reported topic (rules lost after compaction)
